name: Relativistic Discs of Lynden-Bell and Pineault
description: Thin relativistic discs with counter rotating streams or matter rotating in one sense, and a circular speed independent of radius.
convention: Components use $x^0 = ct$, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$, and $\dot t = d(ct)/d\lambda$ for affine parameter $\lambda$, with $c$ and $G$ explicit. Matter occupies an infinitesimally thin equatorial sheet, and smooth tensors describe the vacuum exterior.
history: The gravity of an infinite disc can support circular motion at a speed independent of radius. Donald Lynden-Bell and Serge Pineault constructed such relativistic equilibria in 1978, publishing their counter rotating and rotating families in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society [lyndenbell1978, lyndenbellpineault1978b]. The constants $G$ and $c$, together with the circular speed, supply no characteristic length. These infinite discs are self similar, with a change of radial scale accompanied by a change of the time scale [lyndenbellpineault1978b].¶Equal streams of stars circle in opposite senses in the counter rotating family. Each stream is cold, and its stars follow circular orbits with a speed independent of radius. The opposing streams have equal and opposite angular momenta, and their gravitational field is static, with no dragging of inertial frames [lyndenbell1978]. Lynden-Bell and Pineault also constructed finite discs whose geometry approaches the infinite disc solution well inside the outer edge [lyndenbell1978].¶The matter occupies an infinitesimally thin equatorial sheet. Its surface energy density and azimuthal stress enter Einstein's equations through a delta function supported on that sheet [lyndenbell1978]. The regions above and below the disc satisfy the vacuum Einstein equations, with a vanishing smooth Ricci tensor away from the matter surface [lyndenbell1978, lyndenbellpineault1978b].¶At the speed of light, the counter rotating streams consist of particles with zero rest mass [lyndenbell1978]. Lynden-Bell and Pineault obtained analytic photon trajectories for this limiting disc. Some photons circle at constant radius while oscillating across the equatorial plane, and others spiral inward or outward [lyndenbell1978].¶Matter rotating in one sense drags the surrounding inertial frames. Lynden-Bell and Pineault reduced the stationary field equations through self similarity and determined the rotating disc's angular metric functions numerically [lyndenbellpineault1978b]. An ergoregion appears around the equatorial plane at a circular speed of approximately $0.384c$ measured by locally nonrotating observers, where the stationary Killing vector becomes spacelike. Its conical boundary extends toward the symmetry axis as the rotation speed increases. Their cold rotating sequence ends near $0.438c$, with a diverging frame dragging parameter and an ergoregion extending throughout space away from the axis [lyndenbellpineault1978b].¶The infinite discs have infinite total mass and a geometry that is not asymptotically flat [lyndenbell1978, lyndenbellpineault1978b]. The cold counter rotating equilibria are unstable to gravitational fragmentation into rings [lyndenbell1978]. Mike J. Cai and Frank H. Shu included isothermal pressure in the disc plane in 2002, retaining infinitesimal vertical thickness and a circular speed independent of radius [caishu2002].

related.text: Counter-rotating discs obtained with the static axisymmetric construction used for the Morgan-Morgan discs [lyndenbell1978].
Flat space is recovered when the circular speed of both counter rotating streams vanishes [lyndenbell1978].
